_note: The Noctalia settings this project writes, with the type, range and enum upstream declares for each. Derived from the sources named below at the tag in verified_against, by reading the Schema<> declarations in config_schema.cpp (field/enumField/colorField/subTable/custom and their optional* variants), the Range<> constants in ranges.h and config_schema.cpp, and the enum tables in config_types.h. render_noctalia.py refuses to emit a key that is not listed here.
source: src/config/schema/config_schema.cpp, src/config/schema/ranges.h, src/config/config_types.h, src/config/config_validate.cpp, src/theme/custom_palettes.cpp, docs/user/theming/palette.mdx

diagnostics.unknown_key: warning: config_validate.cpp reports diag.warn(path, "unknown setting") and the parser ignores the key
diagnostics.out_of_range: warning: the parser clamps and continues, so a bad number is silently changed
diagnostics.consequence: Neither a warning nor a clamp is acceptable in a shipped payload: this project treats both as failures at render time.

bar_container._note: Bars live at the config root, not in a section: {"bar"} and {"bar",name} are container levels, and "position" and "name" are keyed outside barFieldsSchema (isKnownConfigPath in config_schema.cpp).

color_roles_note: The 28 user-facing roles from docs/user/theming/palette.mdx. A colorField accepts one of these names or a fixed hex colour (#RGB, #RGBA, #RRGGBB, #RRGGBBAA); role names are preferred so colours follow the palette. surface_variant and outline were renamed to surface_container and outline_variant, and Noctalia rewrites the old names on load with a warning.

palette.light_optional: If light is omitted, Noctalia uses the dark variant for both modes.
palette.field_forms: writeFixedColor emits "m" + UpperCamel; the reader tries the prefixed key first and falls back to the unprefixed camelCase name.
palette.name_sanitization: sanitizePaletteNameComponent keeps alphanumerics and folds separators to single dashes, lowercased.

border_color.color_note: a colour role name or a fixed hex colour

floating_layer.enum_note: custom parser: any other value warns and leaves the setting unset

grid.note: Lay the actions out over rows of grid_columns instead of fitting them on one row.

grid_columns.note: Actions per row when grid is true; ignored otherwise.

show_shortcuts.note: Show each action's keyboard shortcut at the top right of its button.

actions.note: An array of tables, written [[shell.session.actions]]. Omitting it keeps the default five actions, whose shortcuts are the keys 1 to 5; an explicit empty array hides every session button. This is the one place v5.4.1 lets a config file add a button that runs a command of yours.

action.note: lock, logout, suspend, lock_and_suspend, reboot, reboot_uefi, shutdown, or command for a custom entry. Lowercased and trimmed on read, and not enum-validated, so an unknown word yields a button that does nothing.

command.note: Run with /bin/sh -c instead of the built-in handler. Required when action is command. Noctalia runs the string, so it is as privileged as the session.

label.note: Button label; otherwise the translated default for the action.

glyph.note: A bar-style icon id; otherwise the action's default. The id vocabulary is not published in the schema, so an unknown glyph is a guess.

shortcut.note: Any XKB key name (1, F1, Escape) or modifier combo (Ctrl+1), active while the session panel is open. Empty disables it.

lockscreen_shortcut.note: Triggers the action from the lock screen. Keys that type text are rejected because the password field owns them.

countdown_seconds.note: Above zero, the first activation starts a countdown on the button badge; a second activation runs it at once. Zero runs immediately.

variant.enum_note: The enum constant carries six variants; the user documentation lists five and does not mention ghost.

power.note: Command overrides for the built-in suspend, reboot and shutdown, used by the session panel, the launcher, IPC and idle. Each is run with /bin/sh -lc. Left unset, Noctalia tries its own prioritized backend list (systemd, logind, privileged helpers), which is why this project emits nothing here: it has no business inventing a sudo command line.

position.note: Keyed outside barFieldsSchema: isKnownConfigPath in config_schema.cpp accepts {"bar",name,"position"} and {"bar",name,"name"} as container levels, so this is a real setting even though the field schema does not declare it.

border.color_note: a colour role name or a fixed hex colour

capsule_fill.color_note: a colour role name or a fixed hex colour

capsule_border.color_note: a colour role name or a fixed hex colour

border.color_note: a colour role name or a fixed hex colour

layer.enum_note: custom parser: any other value warns and leaves the setting unset

sidebar.note: Tab navigation when the panel opens on Home. full = icons and labels, compact = icons only, none = no sidebar.

sidebar_section.note: Sidebar used when an open jumps straight to a tab (a bar volume, network or media widget, or `panel-toggle control-center <context>`). Defaults to compact.

show_shortcut_labels.note: Text under each Home shortcut icon. Off, the icons scale with the cell, which helps at narrow widths.

show_session_button.note: The session-actions button in the Home tab header. Independent of a type = "session" shortcut and of the bar's session widget.

circular_avatar.note: Off, the avatar follows the shell's corner roundness.

show_avatar_border.note: The accent ring around the Home avatar, including on hover and keyboard focus.

hidden_tabs.note: Tab context ids to hide: home, media, audio, monitor, system, network, bluetooth, weather, calendar, notifications, screen-time, power. Empty shows every available tab, and Home cannot be hidden. Hidden tabs also drop out of keyboard navigation and the launcher's Panels provider.

show_week_numbers.note: ISO 8601 week numbers in the month grid.

show_visualizer.note: The PipeWire visualizer beside the playback controls; also toggled from the tab header.

shortcuts.note: An array of tables, written [[control_center.shortcuts]]. Up to six are shown on Home. Omitting the array entirely gives the default set (wifi, bluetooth, caffeine, nightlight, notification, power_profile); an explicit empty array hides every shortcut button.

type.enum_note: Not an upstream enum. shortcutSchema() declares a plain string field, so an unknown type is not warned about or rejected -- it simply renders no button. The eighteen documented types are recorded here, from docs/user/control-center/shortcuts.mdx, so the renderer refuses a tile that would never appear instead of shipping a dead one.
type.note: The only field a shortcut entry has. weather, system and screen_time need their service enabled to appear; screen_recorder needs the official plugin enabled or the shortcut stays disabled.

position.note: Documented values: top_right, top_left, top_center, bottom_right, bottom_left, bottom_center. This is a plain string field, not an enum: notification_toast.cpp only tests starts_with("bottom_") and ends_with("_left"/"_center"), so any other value lands on the top-right branch instead of being rejected.

layer.note: top keeps toasts above normal windows; overlay puts them above fullscreen apps. Plain string field: an unrecognised value is not rejected by the schema.

offset_x.note: Absolute margin from the screen edge. It is split by shell::surface_edge_inset::resolve() into a layer margin plus the card's own inner padding, so the painted card edge sits exactly offset_x from the edge either way.

offset_y.note: Absolute margin from the screen edge, used verbatim as the layer surface's top (and bottom) margin: no inset compensation like offset_x gets.

max_visible.range_note: inline Range<std::int64_t>{0, 20} passed to field() in notificationSchema(); no named constant upstream
max_visible.note: 0 = fill the available space; otherwise at most this many toasts.

history_retention_hours.range_note: inline Range<std::int64_t>{0, 8760} passed to field() in notificationSchema(); no named constant upstream
history_retention_hours.note: 0 keeps history indefinitely; the sweep runs every 60 s.

border_color.color_note: a colour role name or a fixed hex colour

follow_focused_output.note: New toasts appear on the focused output; toasts already on screen stay put and each output keeps its own stack. Takes precedence over monitors.

monitors.note: Empty = every monitor. Otherwise exact connector names (eDP-1) or word-boundary tokens from the monitor description. If none of the listed monitors is connected Noctalia falls back to all of them rather than dropping toasts.

blacklist.note: Legacy shim. Read only while no [notification.filter.*] table exists; each token becomes a filter with show_toast, save_history and play_sound all false. Never written back out.

blacklist_allow_critical.note: Accepted and ignored: the read callback is empty, so this key can no longer change anything. Recorded so the validator does not call it unknown.

filter_order.note: Write-only. The writer emits the filter names in table order; a value read from disk is ignored because ordering comes from the tables themselves.

filter.note: A named map, not an array: [notification.filter.<name>] where <name> becomes the filter's name. Recorded with type array because the C++ member is std::vector<NotificationFilterConfig>; the on-disk shape is the named map.

matches.note: Custom reader: the first non-blank token becomes match. Ignored entirely when match is set.

match.note: Case-insensitive token matched against the app name (exact or substring), the desktop entry or the category; normalized on read.

match_content.note: Optional regular expression matched against the summary or the body.

bypass_dnd.note: Default false. When play_sound is also true the sound bypasses Do Not Disturb too.

allow_permanent.note: Default true. False forces a sender's persistent (0-timeout) toasts back to the standard timeout.

override_duration.note: Milliseconds. Replaces both the server default and whatever timeout the sender asked for.

allowed_urgencies.note: low, normal, critical. Empty or all three = every level passes.

allow_critical.note: Accepted and ignored: empty read callback, superseded by allowed_urgencies.

allowed_urgencies.note: Section level, not a filter key: it fills in every filter whose own allowed_urgencies is empty. Read only; never written back out.

matches.note: Custom reader: the first non-blank token becomes match. Ignored entirely when match is set.

match.note: Case-insensitive token matched against the app name (exact or substring), the desktop entry or the category; normalized on read.

match_content.note: Optional regular expression matched against the summary or the body.

bypass_dnd.note: Default false. When play_sound is also true the sound bypasses Do Not Disturb too.

allow_permanent.note: Default true. False forces a sender's persistent (0-timeout) toasts back to the standard timeout.

override_duration.note: Milliseconds. Replaces both the server default and whatever timeout the sender asked for.

allow_critical.note: Accepted and ignored: empty read callback, superseded by allowed_urgencies.
